questions: Do you have involuntary shaking or flapping movements of your hands or arms?
Do these movements occur when your arms are held out or when you use your hands?
Do you have stiffness or slowness of movement?
Have you noticed problems with balance or walking?
Have you had confusion, excessive sleepiness, or episodes of reduced alertness?
Do you have a history of liver disease?
Do you have a history of kidney disease?
Did these movements begin suddenly?
Do you take valproate, gabapentin, benzodiazepines, opioids, or any other regular medication?
Do you use alcohol or recreational drugs?
Have you had recent exposure to pesticides, solvents, or other toxins?
Have you noticed difficulty speaking, swallowing, or writing?
Have you had personality change, depression, hallucinations, or other psychiatric symptoms?
Do any close relatives have tremor, poor coordination, or a similar illness?
Have you ever had yellowing of the eyes or skin?
Have you had abdominal pain or swelling?
Does the tremor lessen or stop when you are distracted by a mental task or by moving the opposite hand?
Does the tremor change its speed when you deliberately tap a regular rhythm with the opposite hand?
Does the tremor vary markedly in speed or amplitude from moment to moment?
Did the tremor begin after a stressful event, injury, illness, or other significant life event?
Are you particularly anxious or distressed about the tremor?
Does the tremor improve after sleep or worsen when you are tired?
Does caffeine or another stimulant make the tremor worse?
Is the tremor present in both hands to a similar degree?
Has the tremor been present for at least three years?
Did the tremor begin before the age of 25?
Is the tremor clearly worse in one hand than the other?
Does it occur in your head, jaw, or voice?
Does the affected hand assume an abnormal posture or cramp during writing or other tasks?
Is the tremor present only in a particular position or during a particular activity?
Does the tremor disappear completely when your arms are fully relaxed at your sides?
orders: Slit-lamp examination for Kayser–Fleischer corneal rings
Serum total copper and calculated non–ceruloplasmin-bound copper
MRI brain without contrast, including T2/FLAIR sequences focused on the basal ganglia (especially the putamen and midbrain)
Serum electrolytes, glucose, calcium, magnesium, phosphate, urea, and creatinine
Liver function tests, including AST, ALT, bilirubin, albumin, and INR
Arterial blood gas with PaCO₂ and PaO₂
Electroencephalogram (EEG) with video-EMG polygraphy during arm extension to characterize the movements as tremor, myoclonus, or asterixis
Bedside tremor examination for distractibility, entrainment with contralateral rhythmic tapping, and variability in frequency/amplitude
Finger-to-nose testing and tandem gait examination
Surface EMG accelerometry of both arms during posture, voluntary movement, distraction, and contralateral tapping
Therapeutic trial of propranolol for suspected essential tremor, with assessment of tremor response
Quantitative tremor accelerometry with frequency-spectrum analysis during rest, arm extension, and the provoking posture
served: surface EMG of forearm flexors and extensors
